item.title: China's innovative drugs gain wider global reach, signaling growing recognition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's innovative drugs have gained wider global reach this year, reflecting growing international recognition of the country's homegrown pharmaceutical innovations, the country's drug regulator said on Monday.
The total value of overseas licensing deals for innovative Chinese drugs has surpassed 120 billion U.S. dollars this year, up 36 percent year on year. Upfront payments in these deals have exceeded 10 billion dollars, while the average value per deal has continued to rise, according to figures published by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), at the launch ceremony of a nationwide drug safety awareness week.
China's drug regulator has in recent years accelerated reforms to bolster the quality of the pharmaceutical industry and boost innovation, an NMPA official has noted.
In 2025, more than 2,900 clinical trials for new drugs were registered nationwide, a rise of 18 percent year on year and a record high in scale. The number of clinical trials of cell and gene therapies grew by about 30 percent last year, highlighting strong activity in cutting-edge areas of drug development.
Regulatory reforms have also helped to deliver more innovative products to the market. Since the beginning of 2026, a total of 59 innovative drugs and 51 innovative medical devices have been approved for market, including 13 first-in-class drugs featuring new mechanisms or targets.
Eyeing China's innovative ecosystem, multinational pharmaceutical companies have ramped up investment in the country by building and expanding R&D centers and manufacturing bases.
In March, U.S.-based pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly, banking on China's big market demand for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, announced that it planned to invest 3 billion U.S. dollars in China over the coming decade to expand supply-chain production capacity. This investment marked another significant move by the company to deepen its roots in China.
The NMPA said it will further improve communication mechanisms for early-stage drug development, provide tailored regulatory guidance for key products, and ensure smooth expedited testing channels to support pharmaceutical innovation.

item.title: Chinese, French FMs discuss ties, int'l issues over phone
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Monday held a phone conversation with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot at the latter's request, discussing bilateral relations and international issues.
During the talks, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, China-France relations have generally maintained stable development dynamics.
Facing a complex and volatile international landscape, China and France, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, should strengthen strategic communication and jointly address risks and challenges, Wang said.
China actively supports France in fulfilling its responsibilities as the rotating president of the UN Security Council this month and looks forward to France's efforts to ensure that the council plays its due role, Wang said.
Wang stressed that the one-China principle is the political foundation of the China-France comprehensive strategic partnership, expressing hope that the French side will uphold the one-China principle through concrete actions, refrain from any form of official engagement with China's Taiwan, and send no wrong signal to "Taiwan independence" forces.
China and the European Union (EU) should remain committed to their partnership, pursue mutually beneficial cooperation and win-win, maintain mutual openness, properly resolve current economic and trade frictions through constructive dialogue, and avoid escalating confrontation, Wang said.
Protectionism will not enhance Europe's competitiveness but will instead deprive consumers of high-quality and affordable products, drive up inflation and hamper the process of green transition, he added.
Noting that China is one of the world's largest markets and that China's development presents an opportunity rather than a challenge for the EU, Wang expressed hope that France, as a major country with a strategic vision, will take a pragmatic and rational approach in encouraging the EU to work with China in the same direction, view China's development more accurately, and play a positive role in promoting the stability of China-EU relations.
Barrot, for his part, said that in the year since French President Emmanuel Macron's visit to China, France and China have upheld the "Dujiangyan Spirit" of engagement and integration, sought common ground while respecting differences, and maintained dialogue, with bilateral relations generally maintaining their momentum of development.
Barrot noted that France firmly adheres to the one-China policy.
Faced with difficulties and challenges in EU-China economic and trade relations, France stands ready to promote constructive engagement between the EU and China to find solutions, Barrot said.
The two sides also exchanged views on issues of common concern, including the situation in Iran and the Ukraine crisis. Wang briefed Barrot on the China's principled position and noted that Chinese President Xi Jinping has put forward a four-point proposal for building a new security architecture in the Middle East, providing a global public good for regional peace and stability and playing a constructive role.

item.title: Iran protests as US prevents its nuclear chief attending IAEA meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
The United States blocked Iran's nuclear chief from attending this week's UN atomic watchdog meeting in Vienna by opposing an exemption from so-called "snapback" UN sanctions, prompting protests from Tehran on Monday.
Iranian nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami had been due to attend and address this week's International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) General Conference, an annual meeting of IAEA member states that began on Monday. At the opening, however, Iran said Austria had revoked Eslami's visa after originally granting him one.
"The cancellation and so-called legal justification advanced for it are a stark indication of a political act and advanced formal politicization of this organization," Iran's ambassador to the IAEA told the conference.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the United States had pressured Austria into the move, while Iran and Russia said it formed part of a broader effort to prevent Iranian officials from obtaining visas for international travel.
The United States said it had objected to an exemption that would have allowed Eslami to travel despite sanctions reimposed under the so-called "snapback" mechanism at the UN Security Council.
Eslami was among those targeted by sanctions lifted under a 2015 nuclear deal between Iran and major powers and the United States. The deal unraveled after President Donald Trump pulled the US out of it in 2018, and Western powers triggered the "snapback" mechanism last year to re-impose those sanctions.
Iran and non-Western countries including Russia do not recognize the reimposed sanctions. Austria said it had requested an exemption for Eslami.
"Austria, although being only the host state, submitted a request for an exemption to the travel ban to the Security Council sanctions committee, which was rejected," Ambassador Christian Ebner told the conference.
"As a consequence, Austria was obliged to deny one member of the Iranian delegation the entry into its territory," he said.
US Ambassador Preston Wells Griffith III said his country had objected in New York to an exemption being granted, and that was why the application was denied.
"The United States objected to the exemption request, which per the rules of the UN sanctions committee resulted in the UN Security Council denying the request," he said.
"His (Eslami's) participation would have only resulted in Iran exploiting IAEA proceedings as a stage for propaganda while sidestepping substantive cooperation, undermining the credibility of the very body charged with verifying its nuclear commitments," he said, referring to a standoff over inspections.

item.title: China pledges to continue search for missing Latvians following Nepal-China border disaster
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held phone talks with Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braze on Monday on bilateral relations.
Latvia and China have just jointly commemorated the 35th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations, while the two countries have shared a good and practical cooperative relationship for many years and kept excellent collaboration on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations Security Council, Braze said.
The Latvian side looks forward to further strengthening communication and exchanges with the Chinese side to promote the continuous development of bilateral relations, she said.
Braze said that 33 Latvian citizens had gone missing in the recent mudslides in Nepal and China's Xizang Autonomous Region, and expressed appreciation for the information provided by China, its search and rescue efforts following the disaster, and its sincere condolences to the families of those missing.
Latvia is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with China and jointly handle follow-up work, she added.
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that a sudden ice-rock avalanche on the Nepalese side triggered mudslides, resulting in significant casualties and missing persons in Gyirong County in China's Xizang Autonomous Region, adding that Latvia is the European country with the highest number of missing persons.
In the face of this sudden tragedy, Wang once again extended his sincere condolences to the Latvian side, especially to the families of those missing.
China treats Chinese and foreign nationals equally and is making every effort to provide assistance, Wang said, adding that China will do its utmost to continue the search and rescue for missing people from Latvia and other countries and properly handle follow-up matters.
Although China and Latvia are geographically far apart, the two peoples enjoy a long-standing friendship, he said, noting that China was among the first countries to recognize Latvia's independence.
Since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have treated each other as equals, respected each other and maintained steady development of ties, Wang said.
China's unilateral visa-free policy for Latvian citizens reflects China's trust in Latvia, with people-to-people exchanges between the two countries intensifying and practical cooperation continuously expanding, he said.
China stands ready to work with Latvia to take the anniversary as an opportunity to further enrich China-Latvia relations, Wang said.

item.title: Bowers Museum in S. California celebrates Mid-Autumn Festival
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
A child attends a hands-on art activity during a culture event to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival at the Bowers Museum in Santa Ana, California, on Sept. 13, 2026. The Bowers Museum in Southern California hosted a series of cultural events on Sunday to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival, one of the most cherished traditional holidays in China and other parts of Asia. The events featured traditional Chinese music and dance performances, a Chinese fashion show, tea ceremonies, Kung Fu demonstration and face-changing performance, along with hands-on cultural activities including Chinese paper-cutting and traditional printing. The events also included screening of documentaries on Chinese giant pandas and white dolphins. Visitors enjoyed traditional mooncakes, face painting and free art projects, and had the opportunity to experience traditional Chinese attire through a photo activity. (Photo by Zeng Hui/Xinhua)
LOS ANGELES, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- The Bowers Museum in Southern California hosted a series of cultural events on Sunday to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival, one of the most cherished traditional holidays in China and other parts of Asia.
Tianlong Jiao, vice president of collections, chief curator and director of Asian Exhibitions at Bowers Museum, told Xinhua that cultural events like the Mid-Autumn Festival provide an opportunity for local communities to experience Chinese culture in an engaging and accessible way.
"We hope that through events like this, people in the United States can have a better understanding of Chinese culture and traditions, and that these experiences can help build connections and encourage communication and exchange between people from different cultural backgrounds," Jiao said.
The Mid-Autumn Festival is traditionally associated with the full moon, which symbolizes unity, harmony and family reunion. This year, the festival falls on Sept. 25.
Located in Santa Ana, California, the Bowers Museum features eight permanent collection galleries showcasing art and artifacts from cultures around the world, including a dedicated gallery on China.
Founded in 1936, the museum has engaged in cooperation and exchange programs with several Chinese museums.

item.title: China's services trade fair emerges as institutional platform for open, innovative cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
Visitors tour the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 13, 2026. The 2026 CIFTIS concluded in Beijing on Sunday. (Photo by Liu Zhihan/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- The China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) is turning China's market momentum into shared global opportunities, mirroring a broader trend of Chinese trade fairs becoming dynamic platforms for global innovation and open trade.
Held annually in Beijing, this year's CIFTIS concluded on Sunday with more than 1,200 outcomes achieved, facilitating resource matching, exchanges and cooperation, according to Lu Huiling, deputy head and spokesperson of the Beijing municipal commerce bureau.
"China's opening-up in the services sector provides vital certainty to global trade in services," said Yang Zhengwei, vice president of the Development Research Center of the State Council, who attended the fair.
CATALYST FOR CROSS-BORDER SYNERGY
As one of the world's largest platforms for trade in services, CIFTIS serves as a key institutional platform for China's opening-up and a crucial window for the world to see opportunities in China's increasingly open services sector.
This year's CIFTIS, its 13th edition, attracted participants from 90 countries, regions and international organizations, with more than 1,800 enterprises displaying their industry solutions.
"For Norwegian companies, the Chinese market holds many opportunities," said Henning Kristoffersen, commercial counsellor at the Norwegian Embassy in China. Norway, the guest country of honor for 2026 CIFTIS, utilized its 260-square-meter pavilion to move beyond traditional exports, exploring deep cooperation with China in emerging fields such as green maritime transition, marine nutrition and digital technologies.
Kristoffersen said the fair provides an essential platform for Norwegian firms to assess market demand, match with Chinese partners and establish long-term strategic collaborations in these specialized sectors. While Norway's land-based aquaculture, recirculating aquaculture systems and other technologies in its fisheries are attracting increasing attention from China, China's emerging technologies and services in AI and robotics are drawing in Norwegian businesses.
At the fair, Klaus Hoseth, CEO of a Norwegian aquaculture tech company, showcased a highly-automated salmon processing line. Noting that manual feeding remains labor-intensive during peak volumes, Hoseth saw a solution in China. "Chinese robotics might come in handy," he said, having visited a Beijing-based start-up specializing in both hardware and software for embodied AI robots ahead of the fair.
Beyond technology, CIFTIS is catalyzing a broader form of cross-border synergy -- one driven by China's expanding market access in telecom, allowing global network resources and AI services to better meet local enterprise demands.
As one of the first batch of Hong Kong-invested enterprises in China's pilot program for expanding the opening-up of value-added telecommunications services, Hong Kong Telecommunications (HKT) positioned itself as an "international connector" at the exhibition, with a focus on showcasing its AI product operations and global network resource services.
Mak Chi-fai, general manager of the China Business of the Commercial Customer Business of HKT, said the company is bringing its seasoned international telecommunications operations and AI service experience into the Chinese mainland to empower enterprises to achieve intelligent and efficient operations.
BRIDGE FOR GLOBAL INNOVATION
Beyond showcasing China's open market, CIFTIS serves as a powerful catalyst for collaborative global innovation. This role is reflected by initiatives like the China-Europe Innovation Industrial Park, launched at this year's fair to directly translate conceptual agreements into long-term cross-border projects between European and Chinese enterprises.
Huzur Devletsah, U.S. pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly's vice president and China general manager, highlighted the country's pivotal role in the company's global strategy. Leveraging China's policy incentives and research strengths, Lilly is accelerating the rollout of an integrated chain covering R&D, manufacturing and commercialization, deeply integrating into China's pharmaceutical innovation ecosystem.
"Looking ahead, Lilly will continue to use CIFTIS as a bridge to unite industry, academia, and research partners, accelerate the commercialization of cutting-edge global innovations in China, and support the Healthy China 2030 initiative," Devletsah said.
The collaborative innovation is supported by an increasingly enabling regulatory environment. Wu Xuchu, vice chairman of KPMG China, noted that institutional opening-up in areas like cross-border data flows has turned China into a vital "innovation testing ground" for global services firms.
"This provides an opportunity both for Chinese professional firms to grow alongside businesses and for global counterparts to participate in China's development," Wu said.
Reinforcing this commitment to high-standard innovation frameworks, the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) served as a co-host of the Global Trade in Services Summit at the 2026 CIFTIS for the first time, addressing IP protection -- a core compliance priority for multinationals establishing local R&D centers.
Trade data tells the same story about cross-border innovation. The Ministry of Commerce said that in 2025, China's total trade in knowledge-intensive services grew by 6.6 percent. In the first seven months of 2026, knowledge-intensive services accounted for 53.5 percent of China's total services exports, up 3 percentage points compared to last year.
PLATFORM FOR SHARING CHINESE SOLUTIONS
CIFTIS also acts as a platform promoting China's global service practices, which are transferable, replicable and open to cooperation. Even after the physical exhibition halls of CIFTIS close, its global impact continues.
A dedicated exhibition area for Chinese service cases was set up for the first time at the core of the thematic exhibition, offering a window into the development of China's services.
One example is PowerChina's work on the Kananga-Kalamba Mbuji road project in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where the company integrated infrastructure delivery with human capital development, training nearly 700 local workers and facilitating technology transfer to foster enduring local capabilities.
Fintech cooperation is another area highlighted at CIFTIS. China's strengths in digital services are playing a key role in helping developing nations bridge the digital divide. By sharing digital capabilities and infrastructure, China is helping to make financial services more accessible and inclusive across emerging economies.
"Trade in services is increasingly becoming trade in knowledge," said Benjamin Hung, President of International at Standard Chartered. He added that China's sharing of expertise in fintech, AI, payment systems and digital platforms can significantly empower innovation across the Global South and throughout the broader global economy.
Alongside CIFTIS, other Chinese trade fairs serve as institutional mechanisms to promote trade and advance multilateralism, amid mounting global trade uncertainties.
The recently concluded China International Fair for Investment and Trade in Xiamen facilitated two-way investment. The Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou next week is poised to set new benchmarks for digital commerce, while the China International Import Expo in November, the world's first national-level import-themed expo, is expected to further turn China's vast market into a shared market for the world.
Together, these fairs form a broader network of Chinese trade expositions that bridges economies and champions open cooperation. Within this network, CIFTIS is being seen as driving proven service models into long-term cross-border collaboration, extending its impact beyond each exhibition.
"CIFTIS will increasingly move beyond being simply an exhibition and become a marketplace for ideas, technology, investment and international partnerships," said Simphiwe Madikizela, professor of economics at the University of South Africa.

item.title: Chinese Foreign Ministry highlights key Xi, Modi agreement: China and India should be partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, September 12, 2026. /Xinhua
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi have agreed that China and India should be partners, which is the most important consensus the two leaders reached during their meeting, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry said on Monday.
Xi and Modi met on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on Saturday, following their meetings in Tianjin, China in August 2025 and in Kazan, Russia in October 2024.
"President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Modi have met successfully for three consecutive years, reaching the most crucial consensus that China and India should be partners," Guo Jiakun, the spokesperson for the ministry, told a regular press conference.
The two leaders conducted "a candid and in-depth exchange of views on strategic, long-term and directional issues" concerning China-India relations, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Sunday while briefing reporters about the Chinese president's two-day visit to India for the BRICS summit.
During the meeting with Modi, Xi noted that China and India have different national realities. "We should draw on each other's strengths, support each other, help each other succeed and develop together," he said.
To promote the steady and sustained development of China-India relations, Xi said the two neighbors should calibrate the direction with an objective and rational strategic perception, help each other succeed in the spirit of win-win cooperation, remove irritants with the political wisdom of mutual respect and mutual understanding, and contribute to a better world with open and inclusive multilateral coordination.
Modi said during the meeting that India has an independent foreign policy, that developing relations with China is not affected by any third party and that it will not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities on its territory.
China attaches great importance to the key statements made by the Indian prime minister, Guo told reporters on Monday.
The two leaders have agreed that China and India, as the world's two most populous countries and important members of the Global South, should focus on development as the greatest common denominator, strengthen friendly exchanges and mutually beneficial cooperation, improve the public perception of the bilateral relations, and promote the sound and steady development of economic and trade relations, the spokesperson said.
Both sides have agreed to support each other's BRICS chairmanship, promote Global South cooperation, advance world multipolarity and act as a force for stability and progress in a turbulent world, Guo added.
China will assume the BRICS presidency and host the 19th BRICS Summit next year.

item.title: Xi calls on BRICS to unite Global South, deepen cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday called on BRICS countries to strengthen unity among the Global South and play an active, stabilizing and positive role in global affairs.
* The international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges, Xi said, adding that to bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, and advance the well-being of all humanity.
* Xi proposed five initiatives on "greater BRICS" cooperation in areas of AI, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry, intelligent manufacturing, and science and technology talent development.
NEW DELHI, Sept. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday called on BRICS countries to strengthen unity among the Global South and play an active, stabilizing and positive role in global affairs.
In a speech when attending the second day of BRICS summit in New Delhi, Xi also outlined concrete proposals to further strengthen greater BRICS cooperation, with a focus on emerging areas including artificial intelligence, trade, digital industries and manufacturing.
KEY DRIVER OF MULTIPOLARITY
Xi pointed out that when changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, the Global South, with its collective rise, has become a key driver of world multipolarity.
At the same time, the international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges, Xi said, adding that to bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, and advance the well-being of all humanity.
Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, Xi said. It should be ensured that international law and international rules are applied to all, and free from double standards, he added.
Global South countries should hold high the banner of multilateralism, uphold the authority and role of the United Nations, and support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency, Xi said.
He also called for promoting the reform of the World Trade Organization in the right direction, as well as reforming and improving the international financial architecture to increase the representation and voice of developing countries.
Media staff work at the media center at Bharat Mandapam, the main venue of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Javed Dar)
Global South countries should stay committed to a people-centered development philosophy and strive to deliver on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, Xi said.
Global South countries should also jointly advance security governance, tackle both traditional and nontraditional security threats, and improve global climate governance, Xi said, also calling for working faster to evolve a consensus-based global AI governance framework, so that new technologies can light the way toward shared prosperity.
"It is a solidarity that unlocks partnerships, unlocks democratization of the international system, unlocks an open international system, and unlocks an inclusive international system," said Charles Onunaiju, director of the Center for China Studies in Nigeria.
Rakhim Oshakbayev, director of the TALAP Center for Applied Research in Kazakhstan and former Kazakh vice minister for investment and development, said BRICS cooperation should "bring together developing countries' shared aspirations and promote coordination and cooperation."
BRICS countries should continue seeking common interests, he said, noting that the grouping's expansion had placed greater demands on internal coordination.
GREATER BRICS COOPERATION
During the speech, Xi proposed five initiatives on "greater BRICS" cooperation in areas of AI, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry, intelligent manufacturing, and science and technology talent development.
To accomplish great things and achieve major progress, the foundation of greater BRICS cooperation must be cemented, Xi said, calling for leveraging BRICS' close ties with fellow emerging markets and Global South countries, upholding open cooperation for mutual benefit, safeguarding stable and smooth industrial and supply chains, and fostering a large integrated market.
"We should build incubators for innovation, upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging industries, and deploy future industries," Xi said.
On the open source and inclusive AI initiative, Xi said that China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, support the cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open ecosystem for AI.
On the trade and investment facilitation initiative, China proposes to establish a BRICS special economic zone partnership, under which countries can set up an intelligent portal, coordinate policies, and build a new frontier for open development, Xi said, adding that in an effort to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation, China will hold the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year.
On the digital industry cooperation initiative, Xi said that China will push for establishing a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and conduct digital skills training, technological exchange and industrial alignment, so as to jointly enable the development of the digital economy.
A visitor views a model of Xiamen Metro train at the exhibition of BRICS New Industrial Revolution 2024 in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian Province, Sept. 10, 2024.
On the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative, China stands ready to assist fellow BRICS countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, and jointly promote manufacturing transformation and upgrading, he said.
On the science and technology talent development initiative, China proposes to set up a BRICS engineer cultivation alliance for joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards, Xi said, adding that China will launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation, so as to cultivate more high-caliber talent.
The five initiatives proposed by Xi focus on key areas including technology, industry, trade and talent, providing concrete pathways to lay a solid foundation for practical cooperation among the broader BRICS community, said Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper.
It demonstrates China's firm resolve to share the opportunities of its modernization, a reflection of the spirit of openness, inclusiveness and mutual benefit that underpins BRICS cooperation, he said.
